contracts.rule: CompileRequest is the one canonical request envelope: exact source/content basis, requested products and targets, CompilerPolicy, DefaultCompilationContractId, common execution controls and exactly one typed framework request. No other production type carries compile options.

The typed framework request is owner-local and closed: VueCompileRequest, SvelteCompileRequest, and later SolidCompileRequest (SXC0 contract, SXC2 type) and the TypeScript emit request (TSE1). Each is a variant of FrameworkCompileRequest; no field of one framework exists on another framework's request or on a shared product request.

The exact source/content basis is (SourceUnitId, SourceRevision, ContentId) per VID0 R12, plus the digest of every supplied external input. filename and component naming are Semantic options (OC-T04, OC-T05), not source identity.
Products are a set: empty and duplicate product kinds refuse. Each product names its target. A product never changes another product's admission, demand or keys.
Admission has exactly three outcomes: Admitted(CompileAdmission), NeedInputs(NeedInputSet) and Unsupported(UnsupportedOutcome). There is no silent default substitution and no partial admission.

NeedInputs names each genuinely required external input by type (an external style stage for one region and dialect, a host-resolved fact family). Supplying them resumes on the same request basis; the resumed admission's keys equal those of a request that carried the inputs from the start. A NeedInputs outcome never publishes and never warms a cache.

Unsupported carries a typed reason: an option (FrameworkOption, by request field), a capability cell, a product kind, an unsupported release, or the Optimized policy. Its display text renders each part through that part's own Display; Debug spellings never reach callers.

There is one admission. Every production route (standalone, host integration, transports, verter-tsc) reaches the same admission function, which applies construction refusals, option routing refusals (OI06) and capability refusals. A route-local refusal list is a second admission authority and is forbidden.

Every accepted field is read by the stage of its class on every route that admits it. A field no stage reads is Refused (option-impact class Refused) on presence, including an explicit false or empty value where presence is representable.

One fact has one field. A product kind and a framework flag may not both state SSR; a request-level production flag and a framework dev flag may not both state dev mode; a shared identity field no framework stage reads is refused on that framework's requests.
CompilerPolicy is a closed enum: Default(DefaultCompilationContractId) and Optimized(reserved). It is one nominal type; 'CompilePolicy' in the source plan names the same type and is not a second one.

Public Default normalizes, at admission and before any stage runs, to an exact DefaultCompilationContractId = (ReleaseId of the exact framework release (VID0 I04), target kind, contract revision). The normalized id is recorded in artifact provenance.

The registry holds one row per (exact release, target). A row lists the per-stage contract epochs (parse, semantic, structure, target plan, emit, terminal) and the ids of its intentional divergence records. A contract revision that changes only one stage advances only that stage's epoch.

There is no ambient default identity. A release that does not resolve to an admitted exact release is Unsupported (unsupported-version, VID0 R06); latest, next, ranges and floating tags never decode (VID0 R07). There is no family-wide framework version switch.

Divergence records are typed and pre-registered by the framework lock: presentation-only (cosmetic carrier formatting per the compiled-output conformance rule), more precise source maps, or diagnostic wording. A behavioral divergence that is not pre-registered is a failure, never a record added after measurement.

Optimized is reserved: admission returns Unsupported(Optimized) until OPT0 ratifies an engine scope. An Optimized request runs no parse, semantic, plan or emit work, mints no stage key and writes no cache.
Six stage identities exist: ParseKey, SemanticKey, CompileStructureKey, TargetPlanKey, EmitKey, TerminalKey. Each is a distinct nominal type (VID0 R01).

ParseKey is the existing verter_identity ParseKey (PAR0 G07): (ContentId, language/carrier, compatibility domain, compatibility epoch, SyntaxProfileId). The compiler re-exports it; it never mints a second parse key type (CMP-F09).

Chaining. SemanticKey = H(ParseKeys of the product's demanded regions as a sorted set, the semantic profile, Semantic-class option bytes, the contract's semantic epoch, the semantic admission basis digest). CompileStructureKey = H(SemanticKey, the product's demand-closure digest, CompileStructure-class option bytes, structure epoch). TargetPlanKey = H(CompileStructureKey, target, TargetPlan-class option bytes, target epoch). EmitKey = H(TargetPlanKey, Emit-class option bytes, MapMode, emit epoch). TerminalKey = H(EmitKey, Terminal-class option bytes, terminal epoch).

Each product owns its own chain from its own demand closure. Two products of one request share a key prefix exactly when their inputs to that prefix are equal, which is how shared work is deduplicated; a product never contributes to another product's key.

Canonical bytes come from the verter_identity CanonicalEncoder: one domain tag per stage (verter.compiler.stage.<stage>.v1), fixed field numbers, absent distinct from present, set-like option values sorted and deduplicated, order-significant values kept in order. A key is never derived from Debug or Display text, serde_json, a std Hasher, a timestamp, a process or backend identity (VID0 R14) or an ambient 'latest'.
Map encoding never invalidates semantics: MapMode enters EmitKey only and map serialization encoding enters TerminalKey only (OI04).
Framework isolation: a framework option enters only that framework's keys (OI03). Changing a Vue option leaves every Svelte product key equal, and the reverse.

Cache admission is complete-only. NeedInputs, Unsupported, cancelled, superseded, budget-exceeded and partial results never publish under any stage key and never warm a cache; a stage key never names a degraded result.
Incremental equals fresh: after any sequence of option or source edits and reverts, the warm result under a key equals a fresh compile of the same request. A revert restores the earlier keys exactly.
Keys are value types composed from typed inputs their owners supply. CMP0K defines the types and composition law; CMP1 derives them from classified options; CMP4E keys EmitPlan by EmitKey.
OptimizationRequestBasis is everything known before execution: the request basis up to TargetPlanKey plus the optimization policy revision.
OptimizationObservationSet is the read set discovered during analysis: an ordered set of observed workspace facts with their captured values and one digest.
ArtifactBasis = (OptimizationRequestBasis, observation-set digest, decision digest).
Candidate reuse looks up by OptimizationRequestBasis, then validates each stored candidate's observation set against the captured workspace basis. Lookup never requires the future read set.
The three types are declared only (CMP0K) and are unconstructible outside the compiler crate. No project traversal, proof engine, cost model or cache exists until OPT0 ratifies a scope.
RQ01-RQ10. Construction is the single admission; accessors expose typed fields only.
DC01-DC06.

The compiler DemandSet is the finite specialization of DEM0's CapabilityDemandPlan (P4) for one request: per product, the closed set of required parse, semantic, style, map, planning and emission capabilities with exact reason edges. It is closed before execution starts; nothing outside it does work. Its per-product closure digest enters CompileStructureKey.

RegionId is VID0 I06: the profile-independent addressed region of a source unit. It is the only region identity that crosses a stage boundary, a DemandSet entry, an EmissionSegment anchor or an ArtifactQualifier. Compile-structure regions (control-flow and block regions inside one compile structure) are snapshot-local dense arena ids of a distinct nominal type, never spelled RegionId, never in a key, never crossing a stage. Lifetime classes: Request (dies with one compile request), Snapshot (one compile structure, shared by the products of one request basis), Retained (cached under a stage key), Published (owned by the host after publication).

An EmissionSegment carries no framework field and no identity: its source anchors are (SourceUnitId, RegionId, exact UTF-8 span). An EmitPlan is keyed by EmitKey; under MapMode::NoMap no map work exists.

Every published artifact carries an ArtifactQualifier = (ProductKind, target, DefaultCompilationContractId, TerminalKey) beside its ArtifactId lineage and ArtifactProvenance. Two artifacts that differ in target, policy or any classified option differ in qualifier; ArtifactId alone never addresses an artifact in a cache or a host map.

RuntimeCompileOptions and IdeCompileOptions (the mixed carrier option bridges) are retired; each framework backend receives its own typed request and the host assembly axes (CMP-D12).
Session CompileProfile stops carrying compile options. Its framework fields move to the typed request; what remains is host-level input only (UAK0 S13), or the type is deleted (CMP-D13).

CFG0 CF-H04 experimental flags stay host inputs. The host maps them onto the Vue IDE product axes (OC-P08, OC-P09); no profile-scoped compile key is introduced.
Route-local option refusal lists (refuse_unproducible_vue_options, refuse_unproducible_svelte_options, unroutable_host_request_axis as a host-only reader) fold into the single admission (CMP-D15).
No adapter survives its last consumer. Each MG row is deleted in the same change that moves its last production consumer; no dual-running admission or shim remains.
Wire changes (removing vue.ssr, svelte.dev or componentId on Svelte, refusing unread fields) keep refusals typed and name the request field the caller wrote; they ride the RA01 transport migration.

findings.finding: Twelve VueCompileRequest fields are accepted by the standalone route and read by no stage: whitespace, cache_handlers, hmr, optimize_imports, parse_pad, ignore_empty, babel_parser_plugins, gen_default_as, props_destructure, transform_asset_urls, style_trim, css_modules. The host integration route refuses them. A standalone caller gets output that silently ignores them.

hoist_static is read by the standalone route through CodegenOptions and refused by the host route; Svelte css and custom_element_descriptor are read by the standalone route and refused by the host route. One request means different things on two production routes.

The session compile cache key hashes the whole CompileProfile, both frameworks' fields, with std DefaultHasher into a u64 that is not stable across toolchains, and folds that u64 into the supplied source-space token. A Svelte-only field change re-keys every Vue slot.

DirectSetInputBasis encodes canonical id, framework, is_production, force_js, source digest and project only; framework options and the product set reach identity only through the revision's products_digest of the output. The input basis therefore does not determine the output.

ArtifactId is lineage over (unit, product, language, name). Two runtime-client artifacts of one unit under different targets or policies share it; nothing else on a published artifact names the target or contract.

Three duplicated or unread authorities: VueCompileRequest.ssr restates RuntimeServer presence (the host route refuses a mismatch, the standalone route does not); SvelteCompileRequest.dev and CompileRequest.is_production both state dev mode for Svelte; component_id is admitted on Svelte requests and read by no Svelte stage.
No production site sets any svelte_* field of CompileProfile to a non-default value; the fields exist only for tests, yet they enter the shared profile hash.

The canonical compile_request route refuses Vue requests with non-default delimiters or custom elements (GrammarMismatch) but has no matching gate for Svelte parse-affecting options. Parse-class admission must be symmetric over the classification.

A ParseKey already exists in verter_identity (PAR0 G07) and is pinned by parse_key_canonical_bytes_and_digest_are_pinned. CMP0K-AC1 says every stage key exists once in compile_request/identity/; for ParseKey that must be a re-export, not a second type.

RegionId is VID0 I06. The compiler charters name RegionId as a boundary and CMP2 declares compile-structure regions; those are a distinct snapshot-local id and must not be spelled RegionId or enter a key (NB04).
The source plan spells CompilePolicy and the named boundary spells CompilerPolicy. They are one nominal type, CompilerPolicy (DC01).

CMP1's write scope (F10 amendment) covers only compile_request/demand/, verter_semantic compiler_view/, their registration lines and RA01's seven transport paths. CMP-D12, CMP-D13, CMP-D14, CMP-D15 and consumers CMP-C04-CMP-C07, CMP-C11 and CMP-C12 live outside it. The plan already records CMP1 as owner of the mixed conversion (CCA1T4). Receiving-charter amendment RA02 is proposed to the controller.

findings.finding: VCP6 and SCP6 list only crates/verter_compiler/src/framework/{vue,svelte} as production surfaces, yet they own deletion of the legacy emitter routes CMP-D01-CMP-D04 and CMP-D06-CMP-D10, which live in template/code_gen, template/oxc, compile/, standalone.rs, framework_common/, svelte/runtime/ and verter_session. Their deletion lists name those routes; the paths are recorded here so their dispatch binds them.

TSC0's catalog projections (checker, emit, declarations, resolution, layout) are not stage classes. Each TS option's emit projection must name one option-impact class so the TS emit request derives the same six keys.

CarrierInventory::artifact_identity_token hashes a Debug rendering of the resolved file language. It is a language-crate identity outside compiler stage keys and outside CMP0's successor graph; it is recorded for CPF1 (untagged coordinate/public identity) and not bound here.

The SyntaxProfileDescriptor Requested arm, used for unknown framework adapters, encodes Vue delimiters and custom elements together with the Svelte loose bit. It is a parse identity owned by PAR0's successors and is recorded, not bound here.
